      "observations": [
        "All 98 owned historical diff lines in the one eligible startup file were read. The patch removes both the migrateCalendarUI call and its complete definition. The old helper read calendar.ui.version with a default of 0, returned at version 3 or newer, copied pre-version-2 toolbar customization into the event tab, renamed button-save for pre-version-3 persisted toolbar sets, and wrote version 3 after the try block's work.",
        "Removal stops those future startup transformations and the version write. It does not delete an already stored calendar.ui.version or erase existing XUL-store toolbar values. The author says the last change was in 2016 and thinks removal is safe; the patch supplies no old-profile upgrade test or runtime proof that every profile already migrated.",
        "Fixed accepted loadCalendarComponent goes from locale defaults to awaited manager initialization. Its actual main-window caller awaits Calendar startup before tab restoration. A bounded Calendar/mail search finds no remaining migrateCalendarUI or calendar.ui.version reference; that search is not a repository-wide claim about all migrations or persisted state.",
        "No changed test or assertion exists. The old guard, grouped persisted-state updates and error catch were read as historical contracts, without importing the removed prototype into current writing guidance. Unrelated shared-file sections and Suite-specific behavior are excluded from evidence.",

The migrateCalendarUI rationale is comment 20 and its landing is part of 22.       "observations": [
        "All 215 owned diff lines across eight eligible paths were read. Hidden/main/message windows remove local tasksCommands/tasksKeys declarations. New Card moves to mainCommandSet; the platform-split New Message keys move to mainKeySet. The shared main command include already has a controller-based cmd_newMessage binding, while the removed local duplicate uses goOpenNewMessage. Do not call every handler path behaviorally identical based only on the cleanup title.",
        "The moved key definitions preserve macOS accel,shift for key_newMessage and accel for key_newMessage2; both non-macOS definitions use accel. Current shared keys and the hidden window's include preserve this structure. Concrete main/message controllers dispatch New Message to MsgNewMessage with event versus null, respectively; the upstream command routing and live keyboard event behavior remain bounded.",
        "The compose window renames tasksKeys to composeKeys while keeping its own direct goOpenNewMessage(null) key callback. The key manager only removes an empty tasksCommands set. These local IDs name different roles; this patch does not establish a global keyset naming rule.",
        "The patch also removes customizeMailToolbarForTabType and the main-window cmd_CustomizeMailToolbar declaration that called it. The removed function selected the active toolbox and used onCommandCustomize for event-toolbox. A generic same-ID binding still exists in mainCommandSet and the unified toolbar still controls that command's disabled state. Actual duplicate-ID resolution, event-tab customization behavior and native enablement were not run or inferred.",
        "No changed tests or assertion messages exist. The inspected markup keeps semantic command IDs, consumers and platform conditions distinct. Current scoped Calendar/mail search has no tasksKeys, tasksCommands or removed helper reference in the checked paths; unrelated Suite-specific sections are outside evidence.",
        "Complete Bug 1970022 context is reused by exact ID/digest from the completed 4584 reconciliation. Comment 21 describes scattered command/key ownership; comment 22 lands both patches. The migrateCalendarUI phase, unrelated earlier removals and later final closure transfer no source credit to this row.",
        "Complete D280179 summary and creation-to-final timeline were read. There are no actual inlines or summary/test-plan edits. The reviewer calls the naming confusing and guesses it is old; that is local historical feedback, not a global naming policy. Acceptance, later diff update and landing do not establish runtime shortcut or customization equivalence."
